summary.intent: Implement PR 3 of a stacked PR series for the callisto release command: make a package selection expand to every distribution of the selected package, with matching spec, docs, help text, and changeset updates.
summary.outcome: Created the PR3 branch, implemented selection expansion in release_decision.rs, added a dual-manifest e2e test and ran a mutation check, updated the spec/docs/help, added a changeset, ran CI, then committed, pushed, and extended the PR stack with titles and bodies.

repo: Release behavior is described in several places that must be kept in sync: docs/specs/release.json, docs/architecture/release.md, docs/releasing.md, and the CLI help text in crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs.
Release e2e tests live in crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_command_e2e_tests.rs and use a release rig plus fixtures; a dual-manifest fixture exists for testing packages with multiple distributions.
Selection logic lives in crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs, with selection helpers there.
The repo uses changesets, and a changeset is expected with each PR, along with a CI run before commit.
Work is organized as a stack of PRs, with each PR on its own branch and titles/bodies set when the stack grows.

code.finding: Selection helpers were extended so selecting a package expands to every distribution of that package.
Added a dual-manifest selection test using the existing release rig, validated with a mutation check on the expansion.
Contains a caveat line about selection that needed updating to reflect the new expansion behavior.

workflow: Verify new tests with a mutation check: break the expansion logic and confirm the test fails.
Search for existing fixtures and test rigs before writing new ones.
Read the full text of caveat lines and help output before editing so spec, docs and help stay consistent.
Run CI locally before committing and pushing a stacked PR.

friction: The caveat line in release.md and the help text needed a second read to see them in full, since the first search showed only partial text.
Selection behavior is duplicated across spec, docs, architecture notes and help text, so every behavior change touches many files.
open_items: Later PRs in the stack remain to be done; the transcript only covers PR 3.
The selection wording is duplicated across several docs and could drift without a single source of truth.
